title: How to address selection criteria (with the STAR method)
desc: Many Australian government and public sector jobs ask you to address selection criteria. Here is how to answer them with the STAR method and an example.
blocks: Selection criteria are the skills and qualities an employer lists for a role. Many public sector jobs in Australia ask you to show how you meet them, either in a separate statement or in a one or two page pitch.
Check what the application asks for: a response to each criterion, a word limit, or a short pitch. Follow the format exactly: it is part of the assessment.
Result: what happened, with a figure if you have one.

Criterion: strong customer service skills. At a busy council service centre (S), I handled rates and parking enquiries (T). I created a one-page guide for the five most common questions and shared it with the team (A). Wait times dropped and complaints about incorrect information fell over the following quarter (R).
Use a different example for each criterion.
Use the words of the criteria.
Be specific and never invent results.
